notes:
Big reversal on #1 tonight's results refine, not confirm, last week's alarm: order_status_history shows 100% coverage of cancellations across every one of the 50 tenants printed — Tidewick DOES have a timestamped record of every cancellation, just not in generic audit_log. But matching_rows_with_actor is 0 for every tenant — the WHO is missing even though the WHEN is solid. That's a much narrower, more precise finding than "we can't reconstruct order history." Invoice voids turn out to not exist at all (0 ever), so that's a non-issue; but 85 "uncollectible" write-offs across 11 tenants have genuinely 0% audit trail and no purpose-built history table standing in — that's the real, confirmed financial-document gap. And the churn-session risk mostly evaporates: all never-revoked sessions on all 9 churned tenants are already naturally expired (0 still valid) — so the real residual churn risk is just account status (100% of users, all 9 tenants) plus the 2 tenants with a live API key/webhook found last week.

With #1 and #3 now reasonably well-characterized, tonight I'm clearing Henrik's remaining two questions: whether the "no actor" gap in order_status_history is specific to cancellations or systemic across all transitions (quick, sharpens the #1 story), what actually stands in for shopper MFA (oauth-linked login vs raw password), and who specifically holds the oldest active API keys so we can judge concentration/sensitivity for #4.

requests.title: Actor attribution in order_status_history, across all transition types
requests.question: Is the missing 'who changed this' actor specific to order cancellations, or does order_status_history never record an actor for any status transition?
requests.grain: one row per to_status value in order_status_history
requests.details: Source: order_status_history grouped by to_status (pending, confirmed, paid, partially_fulfilled, fulfilled, cancelled, refunded). For each, count total rows, count rows where changed_by_user_id is not null, and the percentage. This tells us whether the actor gap found for cancellations is a systemic property of the table (same for every transition type) or specific to cancellations. Order by total transitions descending, to_status as tie-break (expect 7 rows).
builds_on: Order status history coverage for cancelled orders

requests.title: Shopper authentication method mix: OAuth-linked vs password-only
requests.question: Since shopper accounts have 0% MFA, what actually stands in for a second factor today — are most shoppers authenticating through an OAuth provider (Google/Apple/etc., which carries its own security), or are they overwhelmingly raw password-only accounts with no backup at all?
requests.grain: one row per authentication method category among shopper (is_staff = false) users
columns: method category ('OAuth-linked' = has ≥1 oauth_accounts row, 'password-only' = no oauth_accounts row)
of those, confirmed MFA count (expected near-zero, included to double-check for any overlap)
of those, users with at least one login_attempt in the last 90 days (2025-10-05 to 2025-12-31), i.e. recently active
requests.details: Source: users where is_staff = false and deleted_at is null, left-joined to oauth_accounts (user_id) to classify into the two categories, and to mfa_devices (confirmed_at is not null) and login_attempts (occurred_at in the window, matched by email or user_id) for the other two measures. Share of all shoppers = category count / total shoppers, rounded to 1 decimal percent. Only 2 rows expected (OAuth-linked, password-only); order by shopper user count descending.
builds_on: Platform-wide MFA adoption trend by month, staff vs. shoppers

requests.title: Detail list of the oldest active API keys (4+ years), by tenant
requests.question: Henrik wants to know if the oldest, longest-unrotated API keys are concentrated among a few tenants/integrations and whether any show signs of broad/elevated access rather than narrow, routine use — here's the actual list.
requests.grain: one row per api_keys row in the '4+ years' active age bucket (created_at more than 4 years before 2026-01-05, status = 'active')
columns: associated rate_limits scope, if any (limit_scope from rate_limits where api_key_id matches)
associated rate_limits max_requests per window, if any
requests.details: Source: api_keys where status = 'active' and created_at < (2026-01-05 minus 4 years), left-joined to tenants and to rate_limits (api_key_id = api_keys.id) for scope context — if a key has multiple rate_limits rows, include all of them as additional rows for that key (or note in the report if a key has more than one scope). Order by age in days descending (oldest first), tenant name as tie-break. Cap at 50 rows; note total matching keys (expect ~76 based on last week's age-bucket report).
builds_on: Active API key age distribution (rotation hygiene)
